Use case: illustration-story. Generate a new reusable environment concept reference for Together Anyways. The attached images are style and architectural material references ONLY: grounded realistic illustration, dimensional warm sandstone, worn deep teal paint, copper piping, desert sunlight. Do not reproduce the characters or original composition.
A coherent small privately operated transport and mechanical yard adjoining this settlement, seen from a moderately elevated landing at the relay-side entry in the foreground. Wide landscape 16:9 cinematic detailed environment. We can read a walkable geography: foreground relay exit down short stone steps to a functional modest checkpoint, a central service lane with a few squat ground haulers and compact NON-ROTOR utility air vehicles, an old low control tower at the far side, and behind the vehicles a neglected salvage back corner screened by hanging teal and tan panels. A donor wreck rests on blocks near that screened corner; the heroes' future ship is NOT designed here, keep that concealed bay mostly empty. Two distinct service terminal pedestals with dim amber displays: one by the checkpoint side wall and another behind a parked hauler, both visually connected with cable conduits to the tower. A heavy clearance machine waiting near a broad side gate with an unobstructed machinery route into the yard. Use a restrained amount of tiny workers for scale only, no foreground heroes. Mix shabby functional old machines with hand-repaired construction. It is a working neighborhood yard, not a huge airport, not a spaceship metropolis, no helicopter rotors. Clear physical paths and hiding cover, sandstone settlement continuing beyond the walls. Crisp realistic illustrative material detail, natural proportion and lighting, no cartoon proportions, no diagram arrows, no labels, no readable text, no logos, no watermarks.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: mechanical prop continuity reference comparison for the realistically illustrated desert colony of Together Anyways. Attached image is a MATERIAL AND RENDERING reference only: worn deep teal paint, copper, dimensional warm ceramic, grounded functional details.
Make a clean landscape reference plate of exactly THREE separate objects on a neutral warm grey background with natural soft shadows, all equally sharp and clearly visible. No hands, people, ruler, text, numbers, labels, arrows or graphic panels.
LEFT, the original old spacecraft flight regulator cartridge: about28cm long, a portable slender ivory ceramic cylinder with exactly three copper collar ribs spaced down its body, a keyed rectangular metallic base connector and ONE small amber status indicator. Long axis diagonal slightly from lower-left toward upper-right so shape, base, and collars read cleanly; visibly handled and scuffed, simple memorable silhouette.
CENTER, its incompatible scavenged substitute: about22cm long, noticeably shorter and squatter rectangular worn teal metal module with rounded edges, exactly two broad copper collar bands around its rectangular body, a visibly different mismatched connector. Not just a recolor of the original. Faded paint, dusty edges, simple recognizable construction.
RIGHT, a small handmade adapter bridging the two connector types: a short copper-and-dark-metal dogleg bracket with a rectangular receiving socket at one end and the original keyed tab at the other; clamped braided cable and two solid fastening bolts. A practical improvised part, visually intact but clearly a compromise, not sparking or broken.
Match relative scale, same camera angle and illumination across all three. Grounded detailed realistic illustration with dimensional surface texture; no cartoon cell shading, no magical glow, no sci-fi gun or weapon shapes, no horseshoe or C-shaped credential device. These are removable repair parts, NOT keys or access badges. Spacious arrangement with complete silhouettes and generous edge margins.
